title: Radiation Pressure
description: Light carries momentum: a beam of power P pushes on what absorbs it with a force P/c, and twice that on a mirror, since the light bounces back. Sunlight at Earth pushes on a square metre with about the weight of a grain of sand, but in space nothing pushes back, so a sail light enough keeps gaining speed. Nichols and Hull measured it with a torsion balance in 1901; JAXA's IKAROS sailed to Venus on it in 2010. A sail pushed by a laser array instead of the Sun could reach a fifth of the speed of light, if it does not melt. Unlocks the Radiation Pressure Balance.

puzzle.goal: Light of power P, carrying momentum P/c each second, falls straight onto a perfect mirror and bounces back. Write the force F on the mirror.
puzzle.name: Light pressure
puzzle.ask: Find F in newtons for P = @{P} W and c = 3e8 m/s.
puzzle.method: The momentum per second arriving is P/c; it leaves with the same, reversed, so the change is 2P/c.
